title: Bounded classical coproduct transport through étale origins
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and $f:X	o Y$ a proper morphism of schemes. Proper has the meaning of [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $T=X,Y$ let $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A_T)$ and $D_T=D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf categories and their unbounded derived categories, in a common universe in which the sites and all indexing families under consideration are small [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $G=Rf_{\mathrm{pro\acute et},*}$ for total K-injective direct image and use the classical-cohomology predicate of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition].
Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}	o T_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $D_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-$A$ étale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For either $T$, every small ambient coproduct of classical-cohomology objects of $D_T$ again has classical cohomology, and their standard good truncations have classical cohomology. Ambient coproducts commute naturally with cohomology and with both good truncations, including the canonical maps $	au_{\le b}L	o L$ and $L	o	au_{\ge a}L$ [def-kun-truncations]. The exact termwise derived functor $
u_T^*:D_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}	o D_T$ preserves all small coproducts. Put $E=Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}$. Assume that $E$ preserves all small coproducts in $D_{X,\mathrm{\acute et}}$. For any integers $a\le b$ and any small family $(L_s)_{s\in I}$ of classical-cohomology objects in $D_X^{\ge a}\cap D_X^{\le b}$, there exist $B_s\in D_{X,\mathrm{\acute et}}^{\ge a}\cap D_{X,\mathrm{\acute et}}^{\le b}$ and isomorphisms $i_s:
u_X^*B_s\xrightarrow{\sim}L_s$; here and above, degree bounds refer to the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Here $\iota_s:B_s	o igoplus_sB_s$ and $\iota'_s:L_s	o igoplus_sL_s$ are the specified ambient coprojections. For every such choice define $t:
u_X^*( igoplus_sB_s)\xrightarrow{\sim} igoplus_sL_s$ by $t\circ
u_X^*(\iota_s) = \iota'_s\circ i_s$. Let $\alpha_Y: igoplus_s
u_Y^*EB_s\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_Y^*( igoplus_sEB_s)$ be the canonical inverse-image sum comparison, and let $	heta_B:
u_Y^*EB\xrightarrow{\sim}G
u_X^*B$ be the value at the bounded-below object $B$ of the canonical natural transformation $
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}	o Rf_{\mathrm{pro\acute et},*}
u_X^*$ of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], which that statement makes invertible on bounded-below inputs since $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then, in ordinary right-to-left composition order, the canonical coproduct comparison $\sigma_L: igoplus_sGL_s	o G( igoplus_sL_s)$ is the following specified composite:
$$\sigma_L=G(t)\circ	heta_{ igoplus_s B_s}\circ
u_Y^*(\sigma^E_B)\circ\alpha_Y\circ igoplus_s igl(	heta_{B_s}^{-1}\circ G(i_s)^{-1} igr),$$
where $\sigma^E_B: igoplus_sEB_s	o E( igoplus_sB_s)$ is the étale coproduct comparison. In particular $\sigma_L$ is invertible and its composite with the $s$-th coprojection is $G(\iota'_s)$. The factorization and closure assertions include the empty family. No unbounded étale/classical derived equivalence is asserted.

proof.text: For either site of either scheme $T$, its constant-$A$ module-sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the small site and its constant ring sheaf in the common universe. Its small sums are exact: write a sum as the filtered colimit of the finite partial sums, indexed by finite subsets of the indexing set. Finite sums of short exact sequences are exact in an abelian category, and filtered colimits are exact by the cited Grothendieck assertion. This includes the empty sum, which is zero. By [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], the termwise sum of any chosen representative complexes, with its termwise coprojections, represents their ambient coproduct in the unbounded derived category.

Exactness of sums in step 1 gives natural identifications $\ker(\bigoplus_s d_s^q)=\bigoplus_s\ker d_s^q$, $\operatorname{im}(\bigoplus_s d_s^{q-1})=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{im}d_s^{q-1}$, and the corresponding cokernel identification. Taking their quotient gives $H^q(\bigoplus_sK_s)\cong\bigoplus_sH^q(K_s)$. The formulas of [def-kun-truncations] now give termwise isomorphisms $\bigoplus_s\tau_{\le b}K_s\cong\tau_{\le b}(\bigoplus_sK_s)$ and $\bigoplus_s\tau_{\ge a}K_s\cong\tau_{\ge a}(\bigoplus_sK_s)$. In the boundary degree these are the just-described kernel and cokernel maps; elsewhere they are identities or the unique map between zero objects. Thus they commute with the inclusion $\tau_{\le b}K_s\to K_s$ and quotient $K_s\to\tau_{\ge a}K_s$, and are natural in the complexes. Step 1 passes these computations and their coprojections to the derived category. The cohomology formula also shows that a coproduct of objects in a common interval $[a,b]$ is in that interval.

proof.text:
By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], on module sheaves $F_T=
u_T^*$ is exact, fully faithful and left adjoint to $
u_{T,*}$. It preserves small sheaf sums: for every module sheaf $M$, adjunction identifies maps from $F_T( igoplus_sN_s)$ to $M$ with $\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}(N_s,
u_{T,*}M)=\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}(F_TN_s,M)$, including the empty family. Apply this preservation termwise to representatives and use [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] on both sites. The induced functor $F_T$ on unbounded derived categories therefore preserves all the specified ambient coproducts, with the canonical comparison determined by their coprojections. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $H^q(F_TB)=F_TH^q(B)$ naturally.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.2 and the comparison geometric morphism; module-sheaf form det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules; derived coproducts: Stacks Tag 07D9

proof.text: Suppose that every $K_s$ has classical cohomology. For each $q$ choose étale module sheaves $M_s^q$ and isomorphisms $F_TM_s^q\cong H^q(K_s)$, using [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Steps 2 and 3 give $H^q(\bigoplus_sK_s)\cong\bigoplus_sF_TM_s^q\cong F_T(\bigoplus_sM_s^q)$, so the coproduct is classical by [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. The cohomology of a good truncation is either the original cohomology or zero [def-kun-truncations]; zero is $F_T0$ since $F_T$ is exact. Thus both good truncations remain classical. This proves all closure assertions for arbitrary, possibly unbounded, classical inputs, without claiming that such an input itself has an unbounded étale origin.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.2, Definition 5.1.3; termwise cohomology and good truncations as in steps 2-3

proof.text: The bounded-below derived unit needed in [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] holds for the discrete commutative ring $A$ by [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. Apply that equivalence to each classical $L_s\in D_X^{\ge a}\cap D_X^{\le b}$. It supplies a bounded-below étale object $B_s$ and a counit isomorphism $i_s:F_XB_s\xrightarrow{\sim}L_s$. For $q<a$ or $q>b$, step 3 gives $F_XH^q(B_s)\cong H^q(L_s)=0$. Full faithfulness on sheaves [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] reflects zero objects: if $F_TM=0$, then faithfulness forces $1_M=0$, so $M=0$. Hence $H^q(B_s)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and these origins have the required bounds, in the sense of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Any other choices of $B_s,i_s$ with these properties can be used in the remaining steps.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 and Proposition 5.2.6 (1)-(3), used through the existing constant-ring module comparison nodes

proof.text: Put $B=\bigoplus_s B_s$. By step 2, $B$ remains in $[a,b]$, so $B$ and all $B_s$ are bounded below. Properness [def-weil-proper-morphism] includes finite type, which includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; it also includes separatedness, which gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] supplies the natural isomorphisms $\theta_{B_s}$ and $\theta_B$. Step 3 identifies $F_XB$ as the coproduct of the $F_XB_s$; composing its coprojections with the isomorphisms $i_s$ gives the unique isomorphism $t:F_XB\to\bigoplus_sL_s$ with $tF_X(\iota_s)=\iota'_s i_s$. Indeed its inverse is induced by the maps $F_X(\iota_s)i_s^{-1}$, and the two composites are identities on every coprojection. Likewise step 3 gives the canonical isomorphism $\alpha_Y:\bigoplus_sF_YEB_s\to F_Y(\bigoplus_sEB_s)$, characterized by $\alpha_Y\kappa_s=F_Y(j_s)$, where $j_s:EB_s\to\bigoplus_sEB_s$ and $\kappa_s:F_YEB_s\to\bigoplus_sF_YEB_s$.

proof.text: The assumed preservation of all small étale coproducts by $E$ makes $\sigma_B^E:\bigoplus_sEB_s\to EB$ an isomorphism. Consequently the displayed composite $C=G(t)\theta_BF_Y(\sigma_B^E)\alpha_Y\bigl(\bigoplus_s(\theta_{B_s}^{-1}G(i_s)^{-1})\bigr)$ is an isomorphism: the factors $t,\theta_B,\sigma_B^E,\alpha_Y,i_s,\theta_{B_s}$ are all isomorphisms by the hypothesis and the preceding steps, functors preserve inverse equations, and the sum of inverse maps is inverse to the sum of the maps. It remains to verify that $C$ is the specified canonical comparison.

source.place: Transfer, compatibility with sums; the étale coproduct theorem is the explicit hypothesis on E in this item

proof.text:
Let $k_s:GL_s\to\bigoplus_sGL_s$ be a coprojection. The definitions of a sum of maps, of $\alpha_Y$, and of $\sigma_B^E$ give $Ck_s=G(t)\theta_BF_Y(E\iota_s)\theta_{B_s}^{-1}G(i_s)^{-1}$. Naturality of the canonical transformation of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] at $\iota_s:B_s\to B$ is the identity $\theta_BF_Y(E\iota_s)=G(F_X\iota_s)\theta_{B_s}$. Substitution and cancellation therefore give
$$Ck_s=G(t)G(F_X\iota_s)G(i_s)^{-1}=G(tF_X(\iota_s)i_s^{-1})=G(\iota'_s).$$
The canonical coproduct comparison $\sigma_L$ is the unique map with these composites with all $k_s$. The universal property of the coproduct thus gives $C=\sigma_L$, proving the stated factorization for every allowed choice of the origins and proving that the actual comparison is invertible.

proof.text: If the family is empty, step 1 gives zero as its ambient coproduct on both sites, and steps 2-4 give zero cohomology, classicality, and the asserted truncation comparisons. In step 5 there are no origins to choose, and $B=0$ lies in every interval $[a,b]$, so $\theta_B$ in step 6 is defined and invertible. The assumed étale sum comparison, $\alpha_Y$, and $t$ are still isomorphisms. The coproduct universal property used in step 8 has no component equations and still gives a unique map out of the zero source; hence the same factorization proves the assertion for the empty family. The only derived essential-image result used in this proof was the bounded-below equivalence in step 5.
